A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SafeDrive work. All 19 pages of each version, including Appendix A–D, equations, 12 tables, and 9 figures, are available and readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original NAVSIM evaluations, Bench2Drive closed-loop simulations, component ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results and supplementary analyses, alongside revised main-text ablation reporting.

M1.justification: The ProposalNet–SWNet–FRNet procedure, losses, and trajectory selection remain substantively equivalent. However, Section 3.2 changes temporal BEV fusion from 'a convolutional layer' to 'convolutional layers' without establishing whether this reflects an architectural revision or editorial correction. PwNC renaming and condensed equations alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use NAVSIM and Bench2Drive with the same driving tasks. Appendix scenarios covering complex traffic, turning, adverse conditions, narrow roads, and pedestrian hazards are retained.

E2.justification: Within Table 5, the reported no-world comparator changes from a fine-grained-safety variant to a control marked '-' under Safety, with a different result row. The named benchmark comparators in Tables 1–3 and collision-avoidance methods in Table 11 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated role of the 50 held-out Bench2Drive clips from testing to validation, retaining 950 training clips. Table 5 also revises the reported safety-control configurations. These are reporting changes to experimental settings; neither establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The world-representation ablation in Table 5 is revised: it distinguishes scene-level and fine-grained safety, replaces the no-world control, and identifies the BEV safety row as scene-level rather than fine-grained. Other component studies, Appendix C analyses, and qualitative and failure cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 swaps the DiffusionDrive-head row's TTC and EP values from 82.3 and 95.8 to 95.8 and 82.3. Table 5 replaces the no-world row's NC/DAC/TTC/PDMS values of 99.2/98.5/96.0/90.9 with 99.0/97.7/96.3/90.1 under a changed safety condition, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Headline benchmark results and appendix numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's explicit prediction-head equations and query-set notation are condensed into equivalent prose. The attention operations, score products, training loss, and Appendix A metric definitions retain their mathematical content. No substantive assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and four scientific contribution bullets retain the same sparse-world modeling, fine-grained safety reasoning, and benchmark-performance claims. The rewritten conclusion preserves these contributions; neither version claims a formal safety guarantee.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly states that PwNC and TwDAC are prediction-derived proxies rather than formal safety guarantees and identifies closing this gap as future work. The existing appendix limitation concerning pedestrians emerging from vehicles and the proposed semantic-reasoning direction are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link and removes the public-code-release pledge; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability. It clarifies the pretraining/fine-tuning epoch allocation and dynamic/static coverage of auxiliary BEV segmentation. Hardware, batch sizes, and training budgets were already disclosed in v1's Appendix B and are relocated to Section 4.2.

R1.justification: V2 removes the Deformable DETR citation and the accompanying statement connecting trajectory-guided attention to standard 2D deformable attention. Section 2.1 also revises Hydra-MDP's described criteria from lane-keeping, traffic-light compliance, and comfort to collision risk, lane departure, and comfort. The remaining bibliography and broad research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the method overview and ProposalNet, SWNet, and FRNet descriptions are rewritten and condensed, including replacing explicit notation with prose. Related-work passages and the conclusion are rewritten, training information moves from the appendix into the main text, and acknowledgments are added. This is extensive editorial revision despite stable core scientific content.

P2.justification: Table 5 replaces its fine-grained-safety checkmark column with Safety labels and an S/F legend. Figure captions 1, 2, and 4, table sizing and emphasis, citation colors, and page flow change. All figures and tables are retained, and the appendix qualitative panels are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves precision through the explicit safety-proxy limitation, clearer scene-level versus fine-grained labels in Table 5, and clarified training-stage descriptions. The gains are limited: benchmark evidence is unchanged, Table 5's changed controls are not explained, and removing the Deformable DETR attribution loses a useful connection to prior work.
